title: Hosted API intake enrichment and priority scorer: automated triage template for enterprise feature asks
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers submitting hosted-API feature requests (chat streaming, tool/function calls, structured outputs) routinely omit operational signals we need for prioritization: expected QPS, SLA needs, data sensitivity, required rollouts, and backward compatibility constraints. Manual follow-ups create multi-day delays and inconsistent triage outcomes.

Proposal: Build an "intake enrichment + priority scorer" that augments inbound feature submissions with inferred metadata and a transparent priority recommendation. Inputs: customer form, support email, CSM notes, proposal docs. Outputs: inferred QPS bucket, suggested SLA tier, data-sensitivity flag, rough cost delta estimate, prioritized lane (self-serve / dedicated / enterprise runway), and an explainable score with top-3 reasons. The scorer will use rule-based heuristics + lightweight ML signals (pattern matching on request text, historical tenant signals) and provide a confidence band.

Goals: reduce manual clarifications by 60% for enterprise-hosted feature asks, standardize priority decisions, and speed up SLA/procurement conversations. Deliverables: intake enrichment service (API + console UI), a triage ruleset stored as config, PM-facing review dashboard, automated suggested response templates for CSMs, and an audit log for compliance.
acceptance_criteria: Service augments >=70% of new enterprise feature submissions with non-empty values for QPS, SLA tier, and data-sensitivity
Suggested priority matches panel-of-experts majority decision >=80% on sample of 200 historical requests
CSM manual follow-ups for operational signal collection drop by >=60% within first 6 weeks
Console displays explainable reasons and a confidence score for each enrichment
Security review completed and audit logging enabled for all enrichment outputs
